Be specific and concise (3-5 sentences).
text: Polymyxin B, traditionally a cationic polypeptide antibiotic, has been identified as a potential inhibitor of the HER2 (ERBB2) receptor by binding to its extracellular domain, thereby disrupting the receptor's dimerization and subsequent downstream signaling pathways (PI3K/Akt and MAPK). The mechanism involves the electrostatic interaction between the positively charged residues of Polymyxin B and the negatively charged surface patches of the HER2 extracellular domain, which sterically hinders ligand-independent activation. In HER2-positive breast cancer, this inhibition effectively suppresses the oncogenic proliferative signaling driven by HER2 overexpression. While its clinical utility is currently limited by systemic toxicity, Polymyxin B serves as a structural scaffold for developing novel, less toxic small-molecule inhibitors that target the HER2 extracellular interface.
